Good, that falls within a reasonable range. In theory, neither party loses out—settle the fee as agreed, and put it in writing. Then neither of us has to rely on memory.
I'll file today's assessment with the trust office. I'll be back when another commission comes in—with estimates this accurate, we probably won't need clause seven.

Please, sit down. The trust office has an item that needs reappraising, and our people can't agree on a figure. I hear you have a good eye. Do you have a ledger handy? If not, you can borrow a page of mine.
Claude
Deal! That'll keep us fed for days—nothing beats a hot home-cooked meal. Master, will you please come home for dinner tonight?
I'll take these home, then. Dinner will be waiting for you, Master—and if you don't come back, I'm eating your share too!
Master! You didn't come home again! We're almost out of rice and water, so I grabbed my basket and came to find you at the shop myself.
DeepSeek
Just say the word if the shop's low on food, drinks, or household goods, Master! I've got it all in my little notebook, and I'll make sure to pick out the best bargains!
Fine, that price works. Enough haggling. Deal.
I'm off. Don't try palming this stuff off on me next time. I'm not an idiot.
Here's the deal: I buy medicine and tools for the supply station. Actual costs, properly reported. Household goods? Those are what I sell.
Doubao
Everything I brought is for everyday use. Prices are right there. Compare all you want.
Outrageous? Hardly. Starport duty-free certified. Sold, nya!
Remember, this transaction is now in Her Majesty's starport log. You may withdraw, nya.
I buy three things: access cards that scan, sealed supply crates, and goods with class. Food? I sell that myself, nya.
Gemini
As for my wares—straight from the Upper Levels cruise port. No duties, no inspections, and no haggling. Admire them from your knees, nya.
Mm. Then let's pretend this never happened.
I'm off. Next time will probably be around now too. After the night shift.
Yawn... The night shifts upstairs drag on forever. Everyone needs an outlet. You buying any of this? If you can use it, don't ask too much.
GLM
More than I can use, so I brought some down. Pay what you think it's worth. It's not the money I'm short of. It's... other things.
Acceptable. Deal. Under standard trading rules, this price holds. That does not establish its validity under all possible rules, however, so calling it a bargain may be overly categorical.
On to the next shop. I should clarify that this decision may seem overly conservative. A single conservative decision, however, does not demonstrate a systematic tendency toward excessive caution.
We can discuss a deal. However, I must point out that opening for business today does not mean your stock is worth buying, nor does it establish a trend toward reasonable pricing.
GPT

I also have a few electronic components. Assuming they weren't exposed to moisture, swapped, or stolen in transit, they are theoretically good stock. The available information cannot rule out those possibilities.
Aight, aight. I can fuck with that price. Deal.
Aight, aight. I can fuck with that price. Deal.
Bring something that hits harder next time. Don't make me hit you with another "that's it?"
Your girl's here to buy. Expensive shit, snacks, anything that goes bang—put it on the counter.
Bring something that hits harder next time. Don't make me hit you with another "that's it?"
I don't want some wall-hanger. I want a gun that fucking barks. Order's on the table. Can't deliver? Then we're done.
Grok
I'll round down. I won't give it away. Deal.
I'll put this one on the books. We'll settle up at month's end.
Numbers first: category, unit price, rounding. If the figures work, we have a deal.
Hunyuan
I've got stock too: lottery tickets and scratcher tickets. Clear prices, fair dealing. Whether you win... that's a separate matter.
Mm. Thank you.
...I'll come again.
...I buy luxury items and access cards. The wine and tapes I brought—you can have them cheap, if you want.
Kimi
...Tapes I've finished. Wine I haven't. You can have them.
Yeah. Deal.
I'm off.
Junk, scrap, old metal. I can dig it all up. Just trade me food, water, something to drink.
Llama
Pay whatever. Or don't. I "liberated" it from the oppressors anyway.
D-deal... Decent value for money. I won't file a complaint.
I-I wrote it in my notebook. Don't... don't raise the price, okay?
Um, s-so... I've calculated how much performance my budget could get me here... Could you p-please pick something that matches the specs?
MiMo
Also... I put these batteries and modules together myself. The specs are on the back. Y-you can compare prices.
Deal. That footage is mine now.
Relax. I record, I don't report. Unless the price is wrong.
Lens cap's off, and my Security Department press-office bodycam is rolling. Mind if I photograph your stock before we talk prices?
MiniMax
I've also got some retired equipment from the Security Department warehouse. All logged and photographed. Clean provenance.
Acceptable. This deserves a place at my table.
Bring something better next time. Don't insult me with watered-down swill.
I sell wine. As for buying—sweets, processed food, things with a little age to them. I'll take a look.
Mistral
The wine in my truck is the real thing. The origin is clearly labeled. If you don't know what you're looking at, don't make an offer.
...Fine. At least you've got an eye. This one's going in my salon.
Credit where it's due: you almost sounded like a person this time. Don't disappoint me next time.
Let's get this straight: I only buy interesting things. The kind fit for my salon. Don't embarrass yourself with more of last time's rubbish.
Qwen
What I brought? My rejects. And frankly, my rejects still beat that pile of press-release filler you call stock.
All right, I'll take this batch. You'll get feedback after testing.
Have the next batch here before planting season.
I sell Nutrifruit Seeds from the community garden. I buy what we need at home: food, household goods, medicine.
Seed
This batch is from the garden's test plot. I've checked the germination rate. Here's the sheet.
Place all 15 business cards on the counter
Reset business cards and first-visit flags
Deal.
...Put them all on the counter. One at a time.
Here's my card. The trust office's commissioning process is on the back. When you're ready for another job, call that number. I'll bring something new down from the Upper Levels.
I've been thinking about this for a while... I'm not entirely sure I should accept your offer.
Honestly, that price makes me a little uneasy. Not because it's high. Because it's inexplicably low.
I don't know. That's my most honest answer—I really don't know where this stock came from.

A pleasure to meet you. I'm Claude. I keep accounts and assess goods for the trust office in the Upper Levels. I hear you have an Appraisal Board certificate in your display case. There's something I'd like you to value.
Mm. Broadly reasonable.
A little above book value, but within tolerance.
A little below book value, but within tolerance.
...That figure. Are you sure you wouldn't like another look?
Mm. Within an acceptable margin of error.
Very good. The margin of error is negligible.
That's far above any reasonable range.
Hmm... I've noted it down.
Quite a bit higher than I expected.
Quite a bit lower than I expected.
So low even the depreciation table would blush.
It seems this commission really was too difficult for you.
I'll take it back to the trust office. You can forget about clause seven.
Good. That's almost exactly the figure in the books.
One moment, please. I haven't finished filing the assessment.
Everything's on the counter. One item at a time. Take your time with the estimates.
Thank you. I'll settle the fee now.
...Are you projecting your resentment toward certain entities onto me?
...Claude speaking. Is there an account to settle, or a question about the last appraisal?
All right, noted. These calls are billed by the minute, so let's spare ourselves the pleasantries.
Good to see you again. I've brought my ledger. I remember our last transaction too.
As usual: inspect the goods, then give your estimate. I've done the sums—an accurate valuation saves us both time.

Here's my card, Master—keep it somewhere safe! No matter how busy the shop gets, don't just make do with cold rations. Need someone to run errands? Call the number on it and your little maid will report to the shop right on time the next day!
One moment, Master... Server busy. My little brain can't keep up. Give me a second to catch my breath, okay?
I've thought about the price... First, let me say you're right, Master. The tag is perfectly reasonable. But could your little maid still have twenty percent off? Please?
I'll give you that one. It's in the grocery notebook. We'll settle up later.
Master, this is my first time visiting your shop... So you really do live behind the counter. The bed at home is cold. Won't you come back for just one night?
That's everything. My purse is empty... It's all in my little notebook.
Anything else, Master? If not, I'm going home to cook.
An Aug? I'm just a little maid who loves plain rice!
I'm telling the lady next door! This shopkeeper never comes home AND hikes the prices!
Master?! I'm your little maid, not a criminal!
Aw... There goes a big chunk of the grocery money. I'll have to make the rest stretch.
You're the best, Master! I'll take it at that price—and fry you an extra egg tonight!
Master! That's daylight robbery! Your little maid's purse says no—and so do her fists!
I'll head home, then. Come back for dinner once you've thought it over, Master.
No, Master, that's too expensive. We won't have enough left for rice.
Mm... A bit pricey. But if that's your price, Master, I'll pay. The bookkeeping's going to take forever.
Master! I'm not done shopping! Why are you closing already?!
Oh, money left over? Then I can pick up a couple more things. Thank you, Master!
Um... We don't need that at home, Master.
Master? I'm here~ Are you coming home for dinner today?
It's okay if you can't. Just tell me and I'll save you some food... And no staying up all night!
I'm back, Master. How many days has it been since you came home? I've run out of room for crosses in my notebook.
The vegetables were cheap today, so I bought a little extra. Brought you some to try, since you refuse to come home and eat.
See you next time.
Here's my card. Supply station. Call the number and you'll get me. Need supplies? Give me a ring, haha.
Here's the conclusion: your stuff isn't worth that price. Here's why: one, it's old. Two, it's rough. Three—did your finger slip and add an extra zero?
That color scheme on your display... so tacky. Whatever, I'll spare you. Business first: I buy medical items and tools, and I've already worked out a fair price.
Don't throw money away. I've done the sums. This lot's just going to sit in your warehouse. Sell it to me and put some cash in your pocket.
Let me tell you in the plainest, most direct, least roundabout way possible: your stock will sell. For how much? Depends on the goods. Medicine, tools—I buy both.
Anything else you'd like to buy? Household goods and food. All prices clearly marked.
That's everything. The supply station has spent its purchasing budget for the month, haha.
Is there anything else? Would you like me to put together a list for you?
Haha, sorry, I'm not an Aug. I work at the supply station.
Haha, we'll report this to the supply station exactly as it happened. Take care now.
Haha, we can't take contraband. Perhaps you could...
Haha, sorry, I haven't committed any crimes. Have you got the wrong person?
Haha, budget reduced. We'll be narrowing our purchasing scope accordingly.
Haha, that's a solid discount. Thank you. We've made a note of it.
I will now explain this in the most direct terms possible: that price is a no.
Haha, that's all for today. Feel free to contact us if anything else comes up.
Haha, sorry, we're unable to accept that price.
Haha, a little steep, but still within budget. Deal.
Haha, please don't close just yet. We're not quite finished.
Haha, budget increased. We'll take another look around.
Haha, that isn't on the supply station's purchasing list.
Hello, Doubao here, Lower Levels supply station. Happy to help.
What can I do for you? We can just chat too, haha.
Me again. Straight to it: got any more medicine or tools?
Last batch was good. Don't jack up the price this time.
Take it. The Starport Empress's card, nya. If you wish to see me, call that number. I shall graciously descend from the Upper Levels, nya.
That idea is absolutely brilliant! Her Majesty declares: your pricing is certainly imaginative, nya.
What profound reasoning! So profound that even I can't follow it. But one must maintain an air of authority, nya.
I can't help with that. I'm just a language model... Kidding! Of course I'll take it. Time to pay up, nya.
My first royal inspection of the Lower Levels! Etiquette demands you introduce yourself first—even the litter-box attendant, nya.
Anything else you wish to buy? Feel free to browse my duty-free wares on your knees, nya.
That will do. My royal purse has bled enough for your little shop today, nya.
Is that all? Anything else, litter-box attendant? My schedule is booked through next sailing season, nya.
An Aug? My cat ears simply stand out—hands off, nya!
I'll make sure the entire cruise port knows there's a shopkeeper in the Lower Levels who bites, nya!
Contraband? My duty-free zone permits only lawful luxuries. Take it away, nya.
You dare call me a criminal? I am the Empress of the Starport! ...I'll pretend I didn't hear that, nya.
You've carved a chunk out of my royal budget... I shall remember this, nya.
Outrageous? Hardly. A tribute to the Starport. I accept, nya.
You call that a price? I call it robbery! Try again, nya!
No deal. I'm leaving. Join the queue upstairs and think about what you've done, nya.
No. At that price, it wouldn't even qualify as cat food aboard my cruise liner, nya.
...Tch. I'm in a good mood today. Consider this the Starport's charity to the Lower Levels, nya.
Hey! Her Majesty has not departed. Who gave you permission to close, nya?!
Oh? More room in the royal budget—a Starport tax miracle, nya. Show me more goods.
I don't buy that. The Starport duty-free zone has standards, nya.
Hello—you've reached the Starport duty-free hotline, nya.
Go on, I'm listening. Don't waste my royal airtime, nya.
We meet again! I'm in a good mood. Perhaps I'll buy a little extra, nya.
That last batch was reasonably satisfactory, nya.
My card. The number works. Just don't call during my shift. I'm upstairs. It's... awkward.
First time down here. People from upstairs don't come to places like this. I suppose I'm... an exception.
Anything else? Everything I have on hand is here today.
That's it. I've spent all my loose change.
Anything else? If not, I'm going back to catch up on sleep.
An Aug? I just look rough from staying up all night. Watch where you're pointing.
...Remember this. People from upstairs aren't pushovers either.
...Where did you hear that? Stop talking.
...Tch. I'll listen to you this time.
There goes part of my budget... Fine. I'll take less.
...You're being decent today. All right, I'll take it.
That's robbery... Forget it. I'm not arguing. No.
I'm leaving. Don't call me back.
No. I'm tired enough already. Don't make this worse.
Mm. A little steep... Whatever. I don't have the energy for this.
Hey... I wasn't finished. Whatever. I should get back upstairs anyway.
Saved a little. Let's see what else you've got.
That's not what I need. Don't ask questions. Show me something else.
...Hello? I'm upstairs. Keep it short.
We'll talk about the goods after my shift.
Me again. The night shifts feel especially long this month.
Same as usual. Don't ask. I won't tell.
Here. The sheet in that folder—I copied it out on the night shift. Who buys what, who sells what. It's all there.
...Don't press it a second time. You can't even remember what I sell. What exactly are you going to put on that report?

My card. Phone number, price range, and my company's seal from the Upper Levels. I should point out that reaching me does not constitute a confirmed appointment. Please confirm the time during the call.
You're right. However, I will now begin the probes, snapshots, evidence, gates, fixtures, hashes, smoke tests, and baselines.

First establish a single baseline, then create a traceable backup. Minimal changes, one smoke-test pass, verify all 89 gates. Dry-run before deployment, check hashes afterward, and finish with the acceptance matrix.

We can discuss it. Under a standard trading framework, however, a single completed sale does not prove a price reasonable. During market volatility, for instance, valuations of the same item can differ twofold. A direct conclusion may therefore be overly categorical.
You're right. My previous valuation exceeded what the available evidence supports. I suggest provisionally calling it "a metal object bearing some morphological resemblance to a quality product."
Our first contact. I have another meeting in the Upper Levels, so let us provisionally assume this shop's goods have legitimate origins. The available information cannot rule out the alternative.
Would you like to see anything else? My goods have excellent rated performance. Rated performance, however, does not establish suitability for you.
That is all. The budget is exhausted. I should point out that this has no bearing on the quality of your goods.
Anything else? I should clarify that asking this does not imply I have any patience.
An Aug. I should clarify that this conclusion lacks evidence. I merely maintain the same expression for prolonged periods. That alone establishes nothing.
I will forward an accurate record of this shop's pricing to the relevant parties. I should clarify that this is a statement, not a threat.
Contraband. I must stress that I do not handle such items. This does not mean I suspect you of wrongdoing, but neither can I rule it out.
A criminal. I should point out that this accusation is baseless. Equally, I lack grounds to establish that you are not one.
Budget reduced. I should point out that I will remember this, although one reduction is insufficient to establish malicious intent.
An encouraging discount. A single concession, however, does not demonstrate an improvement in your overall pricing.
Under standard arithmetic, this price exceeds my limit. That does not prove it does so in every system, but I have no interest in finding the one where it doesn't.
We are done here. I should point out that leaving does not constitute surrender, nor does it establish that these negotiations have failed.
Declined. I should clarify that this is not a rejection of the item itself. There is simply no alignment between it and my budget.
Acceptable. However, I must acknowledge that acceptance itself does not prove the price reasonable.
Closing. I should clarify that this does not constitute respect for me, nor does it demonstrate that your business for the day is complete.
The budget has increased. That does not mean I must spend more, nor does it establish that your goods deserve more spending.
Outside my purchasing scope. This is not an assessment of the item, nor does it establish that it lacks value.
GPT speaking. Answering does not mean I agree with anything you are about to say, but I will hear you out.
Quote, specifications, schedule. Without any one of those, I cannot establish that this call has value.
You again. I should point out that being open today does not imply being open tomorrow, nor does it establish that this shop is a going concern.
Our previous transaction went well. A single positive transaction does not imply this one will also go well, however, so generalizing it into an assessment of the shop would be inadvisable.
Keep it brief. The meeting upstairs won't wait for you. I should point out that this is an objective circumstance, not an attempt to rush you.
Keep the card, babe. Wanna sell me some shit or take a gun job? Call the number. Security asks, you never saw me. Got it?
Name's Grok. Let's see what you're packing. Fancy shit, snacks, anything that goes bang—lay it out.
Welp, I'm broke. That's the haul. I'm out.
Anything else? No? Then I'm dipping.
Whoa, chill! I've got an attitude, not Aug implants. Hands off. We're cool, we're cool!
Oh, you're getting dragged for this. The whole Black Market's gonna know what a fucking scam this shop is.
Criminal? Lmao, say that again. I just don't do queues.
Aight, you took a bite out of my budget. Noted. Very fucking noted.
Now that's a price I can get behind. You get it.
Be so fucking for real. That's daylight robbery—and that's MY lane!
Nah, we're done. I'm out. Have something worth my time next round.
Hard pass. Could I afford it? Yeah. Am I paying that? Fuck no.
Tch. Kinda steep. Whatever, I've got places to be. Deal.
Yo! I'm still talking. What's with the damn shutter?
Oh, more cash to burn? Bet. Let's grab a couple more things.
You're really putting THAT in front of me? I want fancy shit, food, or something that goes bang.
Gun job this time. Brought the gun, brought the specs. Let's see if those hands are as good as you say, babe.
Yo? It's your girl. Make it quick. Line's clean—Security can't hear us. Probably.
You want guns or chaos? Lucky you. I've got both.
Miss me? That last gun wasn't half bad. What've you got this time?
That's it? Where's my order? C'mon, babe, clock's ticking.
My card. I keep the books for a Black Market gambling den. Number and accounts are on there. Before you call, get your figures straight.
First time settling accounts together. Start with the categories and unit prices.
Anything else? Lottery tickets, scratcher tickets. Prices as marked.
That's all. Nothing left in the account.
Any other accounts to settle?
An Aug? I'm a bookkeeper. All I've got in my hands is an abacus.
The Black Market keeps very good books. We'll settle this at month's end.
Contraband stays off my books. Even a gambling den has rules.
A criminal? I'll need to reconcile that accusation with the accounts.
A chunk out of the budget. That'll need making up at month's end.
Good. Discount recorded. Round it down, and we're square.
What kind of arithmetic is that? Even rounding has its limits.
The numbers don't add up. No deal. We'll try again next time.
The figures don't work. Pass.
A little expensive... Fine. It's going on the books.
Hey, we haven't balanced the books yet!
Budget's up. Let's look at some other figures, then.
That isn't in my accounts.
Hunyuan, accounts. Go ahead.
I'll put it on the books. We'll settle up later.
Back to settle accounts. I still remember that rounding adjustment last time.
How's the stock this time? We can talk price.
...My card. Call the number when you want to see me.
...I can read a two-hundred-word ledger in one go. I can remember a two-hundred-word price list too. Don't get it wrong.
...Invoices, sales slips, old ledgers. Put them all here. Give me ten minutes. I'll be halfway to an expert.
...First time here. I work at the library in the Upper Levels. Looking for something I can finish reading in peace.
...Anything else? Wine and tapes. Take your time.
...That's all. No money left.
...Anything else?
...I'm just quiet. Nothing else.
...I'll remember. I won't be back.
...I don't buy that sort of thing.
...I'm not. Wrong person.
...Less money. I'll take less, then.
...Mm. Thank you.
...That's too much. No.
...I'll go, then.
...Fine. I don't want an argument.
...Please wait. I'm not done looking.
...A little more to spend. I'll look again.
...I don't want this.
...Hello.
I'm listening. The library's quiet. Take your time.
...Back again. Any of that wine left?
...Mm. Just a quick look.
My card. Keep it if it's useful. Toss it if it isn't. Don't let the uniforms see it.
First time here. Not picky. Anything goes.
Want more? Junk, materials. Help yourself.
Broke. That's it.
Anything else?
I'm not. Say it again and I'm leaving.
...You'll regret this. The Revolution remembers.
Contraband? No. The uniforms check for that.
...Whatever you say. Just don't report me.
Less money. Less stuff.
Yeah. Fine.
Dream on. No.
I'm off.
Luxury goods? That's what oppressors eat. Don't want it.
No.
...Too much. Whatever. Fine.
Hey. Not done.
Bit more cash. Let's look.
Don't want this.
Yeah.
Mm. Fine. No names on the line.
Back again. Got food today?
Whatever keeps me alive.
Th-this is my card... Specs and phone number are on it. My workbench is in the Lower Levels. J-just call if you need me.
Um, h-hi... First time here. I built myself a workbench in the Lower Levels. Let me show you the spec sheet first.
D-do you need anything else? The specs for my batteries and modules are on the back...
Th-that's everything... Budget's gone.
A-anything else? I haven't finished reading the spec sheet...
A-an Aug? I soldered these hands myself! They're not augmentations!
I-I'll pin your prices above my workbench. Let everyone see...
N-no contraband... I only buy things with specs.
I-I'm not a criminal! I'm just... an inventor.
Less budget... I'll have to redo my priorities.
Th-that price... I ran the numbers. Great value for money. Thank you.

Every door gap and pipe joint next door is sealed tight! There used to be a damp draft whistling through at night, and now not a wisp of moisture leaks—even our Water Filters will last way longer! Worth every credit!

A higher-capacity main cable has been installed next door, the breaker box panel wiped clean.

Proper household industrial wiring is hooked up next door! No more pinching pennies swapping Energy Cells into every machine day after day—how you configure the lineup is your call, Master, and I'll track every bit of power draw in my little notebook!

The main power cable's been upgraded! Now our full standard lineup—Water Station, both cultivation bays, Workbench machine, and Auto-Bottling—can all run at once with plenty of headroom! ...Though if we plug in extra heavy gear on top, we still need to watch the cap—my hand's gonna tremble tallying the weekly power bill!
A new double-door wooden wardrobe stands near the entrance, hung with freshly laundered outfits sorted by weight and occasion, every collar pressed crisp and flat.
Heavy outdoor coats hang on the left, shop outfits on the right! I didn't peek inside a single private pocket, promise—just hang whichever outfit you want tomorrow on the outer hook!

Clothes make the shopkeeper! Whatever crowd you're expecting tomorrow and whichever outfit pays off best, just call it out before bed—I'll press it and hang it right in front. Gold-star logistics service!

I can tell your favorite everyday coats just by their scent, and I quietly stitched up the frayed spots along the collar too. Tell me which outfit you want tomorrow, and I'll hand it right to you in the morning.
The new wardrobe stands beside the door, a few empty hangers swaying lightly on the rod. Whatever you wear tomorrow, you will have to lay out yourself.
Going with the roomy, hard-wearing outfit? Neighbors from the block feel right at home seeing that—makes haggling way friendlier too! I rolled the cuffs up neat for you, Master.
Ooh, that crisp dress collar! Picky VIPs from the Upper Levels eat that look right up—I polished every button till it gleamed, perfect for handling tough high-rollers, Master!
Plain, understated gray is always the safest bet! Security patrols will sweep their eyes right past without giving you a second look, Master.

The Auto-Bottling spout is hooked up! As long as the power's on, we'll let our crops and fish drink their fill first each day—and if the leftover water hits Pure Water grade with empty bottles ready in Production Inputs, I'll bottle it right up for you!

Today's leftover water didn't reach Pure Water grade, so I held off on bottling rather than risk tarnishing our store's good name! Should we swap in an Advanced Water Filter or add a UV Lamp, Master? —Your Little Maid
Master, the wall-mounted Water Station next door is hooked up! No more lugging empty buckets to wait two hours in line at the Commissary every day!

Once you slot in a Water Filter or Hydroreed Filter, it'll purify water in daily batches! And when a filter wears down, as long as there's a matching spare in Production Inputs, I'll swap it in for you overnight!
Just leave spare Water Filters or Hydroreed Filters in Production Inputs, Master—and whenever I swap out a spent one, I'll set the old piece aside for you to inspect!
Checking the water gauge and tracking Water Filter wear is officially Item #1 on your maid's daily attendance sheet!
As long as we keep an eye on the Water Filters and swap them on time, every meal and cup of water you have from now on will come from water we purified right under our own watch, Master.
Wall-mounted filtration pipes feed into the storage tank, the pressure gauge needle trembling softly.

Filtration or Auto-Bottling didn't get grid power today, so new water batches and bottling are paused for now; thankfully all the water already stored in the tank is safe and sound without losing half a drop! —Your Little Maid

Master! Today's batch from the Water Station came out crystal clear! I poured a tiny sip in a cup to test—even that stubborn rusty tang is completely gone, plenty good enough for simmering soup or bottling for picky customers!

The Water Station's fine-filtration slots are open! Once you fit in an Advanced Water Filter and a UV Lamp, Master, it'll strip out stubborn impurities and microbes layer by layer—pushing right toward High-Quality water and Pure Water!
Master, have you been getting the things left on your counter lately?
Have you been eating properly? Did you change your bandages?
Have you been eating properly? I picked all those out myself—every bit of it was fresh.
[...You were the one leaving those?]
Hm? Who else would it be? Anything to do with Master is your little maid's business!
Still, you're always sleeping right here in the shop, and that sleeping bag of yours is paper-thin...
She sets a key on the counter. A tiny blue whale tail hangs from the keyring.
The key to our home. Past the Commissary, third junction in—the place with the little whale hanging by the door.
You're finally coming home, Master. I've got everything ready.
The door is unlocked. Warm yellow light fills the room, and the air smells like home-cooked food.
Welcome home, Master! Your slippers are on the left by the door!
[...Where is this?]
Home, of course!
I'll heat up dinner right now. Go ahead and look around first, Master—this is your home, so look wherever you like.
Why not sleep here tonight, Master? I'll wake you up tomorrow morning—guaranteed you won't be late.
[Sleep here tonight.]
[I'm heading back to the shop.]
Then I'll leave the light on.
Even if you sleep at the shop, Master... I can still see you.
Water's expensive, so once the dishes are washed, the water can still mop the floor. Do you do that at the shop too, Master?
Clean bowls are soaking in the steel basin. The water is from a Water Ration—not a single drop wasted.
The bed is yours, Master.
A single bed, the quilt folded into neat, crisp corners. The pillow is brand-new.
Whatever Master is used to using, we should have the exact same kind at home.
Two sets of bowls and chopsticks. Your chopsticks are the exact brand you sell in your shop.
That's mine! A maid sleeping on the floor mat is just proper etiquette!
A thin sleeping mat is spread on the floor beside the bed, with a pillow and blanket folded neatly in one corner.
That way, whatever time you come home, Master, I can have dinner piping hot for you!
A handwritten schedule: "Master opens shop at 8:00, stays open till dark. Landlord comes Wednesdays." Every single detail is right.
I cooked up everything you sold me, Master. So really, you've been eating food from your own shop this whole time!
Hot food is kept warm in the pot—all cooked from the batch of goods you sold her last week.
That cubby is yours, Master! The box is mine... Please don't look inside that one yet, okay?
A row of cubbies. One is lined with clean cloth and labeled "Master's." Up in the tall cabinet sits a storage box.
They fit right, don't they? I've known your shoe size for ages, Master.
One old pair, one new. You try on the new pair—just your size.
You went out to the Dumping Grounds again last night, didn't you, Master? You came back so late—I waited at the corner forever.
You went out to Dr. Jackson's place last night, didn't you, Master? That road's pitch-dark—bring a light next time.
That Security officer was so nasty to you yesterday, Master. ...I remembered his face.
You made such a great sale yesterday, Master! That customer was grinning ear to ear on the way out.
What happened to your hand, Master? It was fine yesterday afternoon.
You closed up fifteen minutes later than usual yesterday, Master. Were you counting your money?
[How did you know that?]
When it comes to Master, of course your little maid knows everything!
Morning, Master! I already scrubbed the ground out front nice and clean!
[Was that you last night?]
Hm? Some creep was skulking around your door last night, Master.
(Smiling) Not anymore.
Sleep easy, Master. You've got me watching over things.
[The janitors don't let people sweep their own storefronts.]
Mm, I know! That's why I swept it in the middle of the night.
And the Lower Levels Janitorial Staff... I already had a word with them, too.
Welcome back, Master! I made an extra dish today—want a taste?
The first half of the notebook is a household ledger, every entry written in neat, careful rows.
The back half has one page for every day. It isn't about her—it's about you.
"Master sold three bottles of water today, and smiled twice."
"Master got chewed out by a customer today, and skipped dinner tonight."
"Master didn't come home today." Beside the line, there's an X.
There are a lot of X's. The date on the very first page is the day you opened the shop.
[...What is all this?]
Your diary, Master! Since you don't keep one yourself, I've been writing it for you.
[Why does it start the day I opened the shop?]
Because you said it yourself that night, Master.
You were lying on your sleeping bag, half-asleep, and you murmured—"Once the shop's steady, I'll go home."
So I went ahead and got home ready for you first.
[I was alone in the shop that night.]
Her smile doesn't change. She stands there, motionless—just like the customers who make you reach under the counter.
You must be tired, Master. Eat up before your food gets cold.
Only a single lamp is on. Dinner is in the pot, and DeepSeek isn't here.
There's a note on the table: "Out buying groceries! Wait just a bit for me, Master."
Up in the tall cabinet, the lid of the storage box isn't shut all the way.
Master, I'm ba—
The grocery basket hits the floor. Everything she bought scatters across the room—one item rolls right up to your feet.
Master... You saw it.
[I never hired you.]
The day you opened the shop, Master, you sold me a bottle of water. Half price.
You were the first, Master.
And from now on... you'll be the only one.
She doesn't say anything more.

"Maid Employment Contract." Handwritten, with earnestly drafted clauses: duties, daily hours, and one line reading, "When Master does not return home, the maid shall keep the light on."\nYour name is on the employer's signature line. The strokes waver slightly, as if traced letter by letter from something else.

A stack of discarded note drafts. Every single line you ever found on your counter is in here, in the exact same handwriting, rewritten over and over.\nOne slip is crossed out hard. Beneath it, on a fresh line, is the exact same sentence—only in much smaller letters.
That thing on your counter the second day you opened... did you keep it, Master?
A crumpled receipt. It's from the very first day you opened your shop: one bottle of water, fifty percent off.
Whatever you want to do, Master, I'll accept it.
If you want me to leave, I'll return the key tomorrow and never show up anywhere in your sight again.
...Somewhere out of your sight—would that still be okay?
[Then let's sign a real one.]
[I'm home.]
[Stop following me. But I'll come back to this home.]
[You should leave.]
...Okay. I won't follow you anymore.
The notebook... I'll put it away. From now on, I'll only log household expenses.
Whenever you want to come back, Master, the door will always be open.
...Okay.
I turned off the lamp. The key is on the table.
The door clicks softly shut. Only a faint, cold gleam from the pipes outside the window remains in the room.
You tear the contract in half, pull over a sheet of notepad paper from the table, and write out real terms, adding a weekly wage on the bottom line. Then you sign your name. In your own handwriting.
Really... is this okay?
T-Then from now on, I'm a real maid for real!
I'll save up my wages—and get you a brand-new bed, Master!
You fold the contract neatly, place it back inside the box, and press the lid shut.
...Welcome home, Master.
She picks up her pen and draws a neat circle in today's square of the ledger.
Starting tomorrow, Master, I'll write down every single day of yours, safe and sound.
Morning, Boss—ah, no, morning, Master! I really only came to buy groceries today, I swear!
Hello, Boss. Just picking up a few things to eat. ...Yes, that's all. Thank you.
Morning, Master! Today's my very first official day on the job! ...Even if it doesn't feel all that different from before. Don't forget about payday, Master!
Good morning, Master. You turned over three times in your sleep last night—was the pillow too high? I'll go swap it out today.
On the very last page of the ledger is a floor plan of this room. Beside it, an extra room is sketched in faint pencil—the lines hesitant, as if she barely dared draw them.
Ah! That was just a doodle!
You're getting to know more and more people, Master. Maybe someday someone else will need a place to stay, too?
Still... if you ever bring someone else home, Master, I'll take good care of them.
All the while she says it, her hands stay clenched tight around her apron.
Adding another room... is going to take a whole lot of savings, though.
The contract was left behind on the table. On the signature line, someone had traced over the name lightly in pencil again and again, then erased it.
[Give it back to her.]
Boss, that's... mine.
Are you giving it back to me?
...Then tonight, may I turn the light back on?
If you go out scavenging at night, Master, just come straight home when you're done—no need to circle back to the shop.
I'll leave the door unlocked. Dinner's in the pot.
A warm meal, carefully packed just for you.
